role: Senior Analytics Engineers / Mid Analytics Engineers

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Data Quality Frameworks & Observability: Rule definition, automated data validation, end-to-end monitoring, and observability.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour — quality tests, CI/CD, governance, lineage, SLAs and observability recur throughout with no speed-of-delivery language anywhere.
evidence.domain_risk: Demonstrates accountability for delivering high-quality, consistent, and stable models and analyses while sustaining team trust and reliability.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Moderate — no client sector, financial reporting or regulatory exposure is named; consequences are framed as internal data-consumer trust rather than compliance risk.
evidence.collaboration_width: DS/BI/ML; DE/DS/MLE/PO; Business Intelligence; Data Science; Data Engineering
evidence.data_team_maturity: Collaborate closely with DE/DS/MLE/PO for integrated and value-driven deliveries.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mature — distinct Data Engineering, Data Science, ML Engineering, BI and Product Owner counterparts already exist, governance tooling (Microsoft Purview, Unity Catalog) is deployed, and the role mentors junior profiles.
evidence.jd_authorship: Ensure clear documentation (business rules, lineage, transformation logic).
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: hiring_manager — the responsibilities name concrete artefacts (lineage, SLAs, semantic layers) and the skills section is precise to the level of 'medallion architecture' and 'DAX optimization'.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Support DS/BI/ML with reliable data and semantic layers.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: internal_data — the stated consumers are the data function itself (Data Science, BI, ML), served through semantic layers.
evidence.autonomy_level: Support DS/BI/ML with reliable data and semantic layers
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Execution — the verbs are 'model', 'build', 'monitor', 'support' and 'collaborate'; architecting appears only as a past-experience requirement, not as a directional mandate.
evidence.ai_role: Support DS/BI/ML with reliable data and semantic layers.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_enabler — the candidate's output is the reliable data and semantic layer that downstream ML and data science work consumes.
evidence.testing_framing: Build and optimize ELT pipelines and quality tests.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility — quality tests and data-quality rule definition are stated as things the candidate builds and owns, not tools listed in a skills inventory.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Demonstrates accountability for delivering high-quality, consistent, and stable models and analyses while sustaining team trust and reliability.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High — trust, reliability, governance, lineage and risk communication recur as a register throughout; the fear is unreliable models eroding downstream consumers' trust.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Building and optimizing large-scale models, ensuring performance, consistency, and governance.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mixed — 'build' new pipelines and models is paired throughout with optimising, monitoring and tuning what already exists.
evidence.language_gate: Language Skills: Proficiency in English at a minimum B2 level or higher.
evidence.loss_aversion: 'Monitor datasets, quality, SLAs, and performance' plus 'proactively communicates risks to maintain smooth operations' — reliability and risk surfacing are recurring framings of the role's value.
